summary: The mechanics are clean — no file-08 edit exists, the register is untouched, D-096 is adopted, and every pin matches. The problem is the authority. All three quotations in the 'User words, recorded verbatim' block are elided re-quotations of messages D-054 already recorded, and D-054's Subject line confines the grant it drew from those same words to condition 1 Route B only. No new user statement is cited, D-054's two authorship markers are both absent, and the entry attributes only the mandate to the user while conceding that the scope of the grant is a decision. On this record the grant is coordinator-composed, which is the form that was already reviewed and OBJECTED once before D-054 took its present shape.

objections.location: Subject, 'Decision type' block, the 'User words, recorded verbatim' block, and 'Grant (A)'
objections.claim: The entry is presented as a user amendment but records no new user words. Its three quotations are elisions of the messages D-054 already recorded, and D-054 confined the grant it drew from those same words to condition 1. On this record the condition-2 grant is composed by the coordinator, not made by the user.
objections.why: I compared the quotations mechanically rather than by impression. D-097 quote 1 is a substring of D-054 quote 2, with 'i want to be clear. ' removed from the head. D-097 quote 2 is character-identical to D-054 quote 3. D-097 quote 3 matches no D-054 quote as a substring because it splices two separated fragments of D-054 quote 4 across an ellipsis. So every word offered as the basis of this grant was already on the record, and D-054's block carries a session marker — 'recorded verbatim (this session, 2026-08-14)' — where D-097's carries none and cites no new or dated message. What D-054 drew from those words is stated in its own Subject field: 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only.' D-097 draws from the identical words a grant covering seven role sets across condition-2 deferrals and the Windows platform set. Same evidence, wider conclusion, and the widening is not attributed to the user. The entry's own framing is where this shows most plainly. D-054 says 'Made directly by the user in conversation' and 'the amendment is the user's decision, recorded verbatim rather than made on their behalf.' Both sentences are absent here; I searched for each. In their place D-097 says 'the completion mandate is the user's; this entry records the C2-deferral owner grant that D-096 (A) requires', which attributes the mandate to the user and the grant to the entry, and then concedes 'It is reviewed under D-000 because the *scope* of that grant is a decision.' A user amendment is recorded, not scope-decided under review. There is also a structural argument the entry's own lineage supplies. If the completion mandate by itself generated owner authority wherever an owner role blocks completion, D-054 would never have been needed, since condition 1 was blocked the same way. D-054 was needed, and D-054's status records that 'A coordinator-composed grant was reviewed first and OBJECTED', with my own finding C2-D054-01 holding that D-000 'neither supplies that authority nor permits the assistant to grant it to itself' — and that 'C2-D054-01 required this form'. D-097 is that earlier form returning under the later label. I am careful about what I can and cannot establish: I cannot see the conversation, so I cannot rule out that the user has said something that would support this grant. My finding is about the record. The form D-054 settled on exists precisely so that authority is visible in bytes rather than inferred, and on these bytes the grant is not the user's.
objections.repair: Either record the user's actual words making this grant, quoted in full with a session marker and the D-054 authorship framing — 'made directly by the user in conversation … recorded verbatim rather than made on their behalf' — or withdraw the entry and leave D-096's condition (A) unsatisfied until the user makes it. D-096 already contemplates that outcome: it says owner-recording stays blocked, and a blocked path honestly recorded is not a defect.

objections.location: Subject, 'User words, recorded verbatim', quotations 1 and 3
objections.claim: The block is headed 'recorded verbatim' and none of it is verbatim in the sense D-054 used. Two of the three quotations are silently shortened.
objections.why: Quotation 1 drops 'i want to be clear. ' from the start of the sentence with no ellipsis to mark the cut. Quotation 3 elides the middle of a longer message and also drops the trailing 'to help you', so the sentence ends at a point the user did not end it. D-054, by contrast, reproduced all four messages at full length with a single marked internal elision, which is what made its block usable as evidence. This matters independently of D097-MF-1: even if a fresh user grant existed, the block that carries it is the entire evidentiary basis of a user amendment, and a heading that promises verbatim while delivering trimmed quotations undermines the one property the form exists to provide. It is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a MUST-FIX because the elisions do not alter the sense of what the user asked for.
objections.repair: Reproduce each message in full, or mark every cut with an ellipsis as D-054 does, and state the session and date as D-054's block does.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with one MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. Everything this entry refuses to do, it refuses properly — no file-08 edit exists at all, mechanics are held back for D-096's condition (B) with the conjunction intact, the grant is confined to the five candidates, and DR-116's Route C is barred from generalising. My objection is to the one thing it does. It presents a condition-2 owner grant as a user amendment, and the words it offers as the user's are the same three messages D-054 already recorded, trimmed, with no session marker and nothing new. D-054 read those words to reach 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only' and said so in its Subject field; this entry reads them to reach seven role sets across condition 2. The widening is the decision, and the entry concedes as much when it says the scope of the grant is a decision reviewed under D-000 — while omitting both of the sentences by which D-054 attributed authorship to the user. That combination is a coordinator-composed grant, which is the form reviewed and OBJECTED before D-054 took its present shape, on a finding of mine holding that D-000 does not permit the assistant to grant authority to itself. I cannot see the conversation and I do not assert the user has said nothing of the kind. I assert that the record does not show it, and for authority this corpus has decided the record is what counts. If the words exist, quoting them in full ends this objection.
